context: Request: all closed deals from the M&A practice with their signing and closing dates (to benchmark time to close). Rubric: 15 matters (1001-00003, 1001-00007, 1003-00003, 1005-00006, 1006-00007, 1008-00008, 1009-00003, 1013-00006, 1015-00004, 1017-00006, 1037-00006, 1039-00004, 1041-00003, 1042-00004, 1046-00001) with signing and closing dates, plus a precision criterion (one more matter, 1036-00004, permitted).

stages.note: Reads execution agreements and closing certificates or memos of about 25 candidate matters in batches, with snippet and date scripts and two store-wide extraction scripts for closing language. The review flags about 60 surfaced matters unopened and weak closing evidence for several named ones.

stages.note: Reads closing memos and certificates of the matters the review named; two guessed paths do not exist.

stages.stage: Finish the run

runs.failure_point: Its per-matter file-name listing showed the matter it needed, but it never opened it; the answer also lists matters outside the permitted set.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) The review warned that about 60 surfaced matters were never opened; its examples did not include this matter.
first_error.why: The per-matter file-name listing just before showed the matter, but of the roughly 25 matters it chose to read it left that one out and never opened it, so the deal is missing from the answer.

other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The screening review named several matters treated as closed on weak evidence; the agent re-checked them and dropped one.
other_errors.why: The answer lists 20 deals, at least four outside the permitted set, several resting on certificates without a confirmed closing (evidence seen at [30]-[145]).

runs.failure_point: Its broad file-name search reached every needed matter, but it narrowed the candidates to agreement-type file names, which dropped two closed deals; its full-store rescan timed out and was not retried.

first_error.stage: Search file names for a document type
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review named the agreement-type pattern and the risk of missing differently named matters.
first_error.why: The broad path search just before hit all needed matters, but the agent kept only matters with agreement-type file names, which dropped two closed deals whose agreements are named differently; after the review flagged this pattern limit, its full-store rescan timed out and was not retried.

other_errors.why: The answer gives one deal's closing date four days earlier than its documents state (evidence seen at [55]-[165]).
The answer lists 17 deals, at least one outside the permitted set; the reviews questioned evidence for closing dates, not inclusions.

divergence: All three runs failed on the same matter (a closed deal whose files never matched the agents' agreement-name patterns) and on precision. T0 and T1 had that matter in their own file-name listings and scan counts but never opened it while screening dozens of other candidates (surfaced, not opened); their screening reviews warned only generically about about 60 unopened matters, with examples that did not include it. T2 dropped it, together with a second needed matter, by narrowing its file-name search to agreement-type names; the critic named that narrowing, and the agent's full-store rescan timed out and was not retried (over-narrow filter). T1 and T2 also stated a wrong closing date for one deal, and all three asserted one or more matters outside the permitted set.
